summary: Bidirectional walk completed over instruction.md, /app/sovereign-lb/docs, and tests/test_outputs.py. Blocking gaps remain: instruction names graded binaries under bin/ while the verifier requires build/bin; same-revision/different-body conflict semantics are graded as 409 but underspecified; material LKG-on-candidate-failure, PROXY at-most-once, drain-deadline, and failed-generation non-reuse obligations are in the solver-visible contract but not meaningfully asserted.

evidence.observation: Twenty functional bullets: workspace/binary build paths under /app/sovereign-lb/bin/*, validation/authority/snapshot/protocol/quorum/persistence/proxy/selection/eligibility/drain/PROXY/recovery/observability/lab/exclusions, plus follow-all-docs and idempotent ops.

Delegated contracts cover architecture, configuration, control protocol, dataplane, lab, observability (/v1/status|/v1/audit|/metrics, dataplane /status connections), operations (HTTP apply codes), recovery (authority.json, padded generation dirs, CURRENT fallback), and rollout-state (phases, LKG, non-reuse of failed generation numbers).
Stock build emits lb-control-plane, lbctl, and lb-dataplane under $root/build/bin, not under bin/.
bin/* control/dataplane/lbctl entries are wrappers that exec $root/build/bin/*; graded artifacts are therefore distinct from the paths named in instruction.md.

Four P2P and forty F2P behavioral tests. CONTROL/DATAPLANE/LBCTL resolve to ROOT/build/bin/*. Readiness asserts GET /ready. Authority, canonical digest, quorum, stream limits, eligibility, recovery, audit, and metrics-label cases are present; no assert for PROXY at-most-once, drain deadline expiry, prepare-failed LKG retention after a prior active generation, or failed-generation number non-reuse.
Used only for F2P/P2P classification alignment with test names; not used as coverage rationale.

Instruction owns material functional ask; docs may hold protocol/schema detail; grading-relevant ambiguity and untested material requirements fail Q4; paths graded by the verifier must be discoverable.

findings.criterion: Every substantive verifier behavior must be discoverable from the solver-visible contract without phantom graded paths
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction tells solvers to build /app/sovereign-lb/bin/{lb-control-plane,lbctl,lb-dataplane,lab}, but the verifier session fixture and P2P binary checks require /app/sovereign-lb/build/bin/{lb-control-plane,lbctl,lb-dataplane}. A solver that installs real binaries only at the instructed bin/ paths (replacing wrappers) fails grading even if behavior is correct.
findings.minimal_remediation: Align instruction (and operations prose if needed) with the graded artifact paths under /app/sovereign-lb/build/bin, or change the verifier to grade the instructed bin/ paths consistently.
findings.regression_risk: Low if limited to path wording/assertions; do not weaken behavioral checks.

findings.criterion: Grading-relevant statements must be unambiguous for accepted mutation/fencing behavior
findings.why_it_matters: Verifier requires HTTP 409 when the accepted revision is reused with a different body and a different idempotency key. Instruction/operations explicitly name stale (lower) revisions and idempotency-key body conflicts, not equal-revision/different-body/different-key. Solvers can reasonably choose another status or acceptance rule and still believe they satisfied the published fence.
findings.minimal_remediation: State in solver-visible material that an accepted revision must strictly increase for a new body, and that equal revision with different content is a 409 conflict regardless of idempotency key.
findings.regression_risk: Low; clarifies existing intended fence without changing domain scope.

findings.criterion: Every material requirement must have meaningful behavioral coverage
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires prepare/activate coordination without damaging the last active generation when a candidate fails. Existing tests either reject before a candidate is accepted (409 conflict) or show a first rollout that never becomes active under insufficient quorum. Neither asserts that an already-active generation remains serving after a later accepted candidate fails prepare/activate.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add an F2P case: activate generation N, accept a later revision that cannot reach prepare/activate quorum (or is rejected mid-rollout), and assert active_generation/listeners remain N.
findings.regression_risk: Low; adds coverage for an already-stated invariant.

findings.criterion: Every material requirement must have meaningful behavioral coverage
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction and dataplane.md require at most one valid PROXY protocol v2 header per backend connection. The only PROXY test checks that payload echoes through the inspect listener; it does not assert header count/identity or reject double-header emission on a single established backend.
findings.minimal_remediation: Extend PROXY coverage to assert exactly one v2 header on first backend establish and no second header on the same established backend (lab inspect events or equivalent).
findings.regression_risk: Low if anchored on existing inspect backend semantics.

findings.criterion: Material drain/deadline obligations on the stable dataplane contract must be tested
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires owned connections to drain until their deadline. The drain test only shows continued service for an existing owner and new traffic moving to the replacement target; it never asserts forced teardown when drain_timeout_ms elapses. Deadline enforcement can be omitted while still passing.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a behavioral case with a short drain_timeout_ms that proves the owned stream is terminated by the deadline after deregister/drain.
findings.regression_risk: Medium timing sensitivity; keep timeouts deterministic and generous relative to poll intervals.

findings.criterion: Delegated stable public-interface obligations must be covered when instruction incorporates docs by reference
findings.why_it_matters: rollout-state.md states a later apply may create a new generation but cannot reuse a failed generation number. Instruction requires following docs contracts. No verifier assertion checks generation monotonic non-reuse after rejected/aborted candidates, so solvers can violate a documented allocator rule unnoticed.
findings.minimal_remediation: After a failed/aborted candidate, accept a new revision and assert the new generation id is strictly greater and does not reuse the failed number.

findings.criterion: Stable HTTP readiness path should be named in technical docs
findings.why_it_matters: Verifier grades GET /ready, but docs only say management readiness is exposed as JSON without naming the path. Discoverable via lbctl, so not blocking, but docs/API surface are incomplete.
findings.minimal_remediation: Name GET /ready (and ready JSON shape) in observability/operations.

findings.criterion: Fence dimensions called out in instruction should preferably have direct assertions
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction fences acknowledgements by node identity, session identity, generation, digest, and sequence. Tests cover session mismatch, sequence reuse, and torn frames; node-id and digest/generation mismatch acknowledgements are not separately asserted.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optionally add focused control-plane probes for node_id and digest/generation mismatch rejection without quorum advance.

findings.criterion: Negative exclusions and language-structure preservation are stated but not graded
findings.why_it_matters: No-HTTP-routing/WAF/DNS/firewall/cloud exclusions and preserve Go/C++/Bash/Python structure are work-request constraints without behavioral assertions. Non-blocking for this large-system profile unless later graded.
findings.minimal_remediation: Leave as advisory scope limits, or add lightweight presence checks only if those constraints become graded.
